players.product: single-mode optical fiber and MPO fiber cable for AI data center interconnects

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: Q2 2026 was 'the best quarter ever of Prysmian' with EUR 730 million EBITDA, a 13.4% EBITDA margin (15.4% at standard metal, per CFO Pier Francesco) and 9.4% organic growth. Transmission EBITDA was EUR 180 million at a 21.2% margin with 14.3% organic growth, almost EUR 60 million above the same quarter last year; Power Grid EBITDA was EUR 135 million, its margin rebounding sequentially from 12.4% to 13.8%, with 13% organic growth on strong US and European demand; Industrial & Construction EBITDA was EUR 128 million, with US organic growth of 13.4% driven by data centers and an improving residential market and June the strongest month ever; Digital Solutions EBITDA margin reached 24% from 20.6% in Q1, and of its EUR 60 million year-on-year increase EUR 30 million came from consolidating Channell for the full period; Specialties remained weak (elevators, oil and gas, automotive). CFO: H1 organic growth was in excess of 7% and H1 group net profit reached EUR 569 million, the highest ever.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 EBITDA EUR 730 million; organic growth 9.4%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: the hyperscaler and Molex deals bring EUR 10 billion of incremental revenues in the optical space over the next 10 years. Molex accounts for EUR 5.5 billion under a 10-year deal signed about three weeks before the call; the balance is with hyperscalers or players in the infrastructure deployment of data centers, shorter in duration and covered for the next five to six years by deals already signed. The contracts carry guaranteed volume (take-or-pay), a formula passing cost changes through at the end of each quarter and a guaranteed margin per fiber sold over the whole period; margins are pretty much the same for Molex and the hyperscalers, and newer deals carry better margins. Molex pays a EUR 550 million down payment in H2 2026 (CFO), the vast majority of which Prysmian gives back in 2030-2033 as deliveries proceed. The CEO feels pretty confident of signing new deals over the next two quarters, a second wave over and above the EUR 10 billion that would need additional capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 10 billion incremental optical revenues over 10 years; Molex EUR 5.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: Digital Solutions revenue was EUR 1.6 billion in 2025, of which about EUR 600 million optical (about EUR 200 million of it data center) and the rest roughly equally split between connectivity and MMS (copper cables). The new deals add EUR 1.1 billion of incremental data-center revenue, equal to the added capacity, reaching full run rate in 2030; with fiber-to-the-home volume being reallocated to data centers, optical revenue should reach EUR 1.7 billion by 2030 with EUR 1.5 billion (85%-90%) from data centers. The Digital Solutions EBITDA margin should end Q4 2026 slightly higher than 25%, with H1 probably at 22.5%-23%, and rise linearly from 2027 through 2028 to between 25% and 30%; repricing of the old business adds 'easily EUR 50 million, EUR 70 million, EUR 80 million' to the previous guidance, with contracts and frame agreements renegotiated every week. Channell's connectivity business runs at a 36%-37% EBITDA margin and is developing larger underground boxes for data-center applications.
quarterly_data.figure: 2030 optical revenue EUR 1.7 billion, of which EUR 1.5 billion data center

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: the fiber shortage will continue until 2029, and he personally believes the imbalance will continue beyond 2029; Prysmian's fiber capacity is still what it was one year ago and will remain unchanged for the next two years, so 'every single week we are disappointing customer because we have no fiber to give them'. The players building US fiber capacity are Prysmian and Corning, as US-origin fiber is needed to avoid the tariff on fiber produced in China. In Power Grid, Prysmian is 'currently flat out in terms of capacity in Europe and North America'.

CEO Massimo Battaini: Prysmian plans to more than double its fiber capacity located in the US by 2029, with one third to 40% of the run-rate capacity in place by 2028; part of the capacity increase happens in Europe in 2027, and marginal debottlenecking of existing capacity adds volume in 2027. A further capacity expansion beyond what was committed for Molex and the others is being considered with hyperscalers or other infrastructure players. In Power Grid, additional megawatt capacity was approved in the US and Europe one year ago and another wave in the US two months ago, serving Industrial & Construction (EPC or data-center expansion) and utilities. CFO Pier Francesco: capex accelerates in 2026 by approximately EUR 200 million over the level embedded in the guidance, and the CEO said capex continues stronger in 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex approximately EUR 200 million above the guidance level

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: Prysmian has 'super high confidence' of reaching EUR 2.850 billion of 2026 EBITDA and ending in the upper part of the raised range, at EUR 2.850-EUR 2.9 billion, already close to the 2028 target set at the 2025 Capital Markets Day; Transmission will add EUR 200 million of EBITDA to last year's EUR 580 million. Free cash flow guidance of EUR 1.7 billion is the highest ever and includes the EUR 550 million Molex down payment; CFO Pier Francesco: higher EBITDA and working capital offset a metal-price impact of around EUR 250 million versus the original guidance. CFO: the 2026 group net profit estimate is in excess of EUR 1.2 billion, and year-end net debt should be in the region of EUR 2.3 billion-EUR 2.4 billion, a leverage of around 0.8 times.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 group net profit in excess of EUR 1.2 billion; year-end net debt EUR 2.3 billion-EUR 2.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: the Transmission backlog is 'still pretty high, EUR 17 billion'; Prysmian estimates around EUR 10 billion of new projects awarded to the market in 2026 and expects that level to be beaten in 2027 and 2028, with the second half a bit more buoyant than the first. Power Grid margins trail the record of a year ago only because cost increases pass through with a time lag amid inflation and the Iran war; the market is 'super strong' with no pricing pressure, and the CEO expects to restore the 14.5% or 15% EBITDA margin in Q4 or Q1.

CEO Massimo Battaini: since US tariffs on aluminum cable moved from 50% on the metal to 25% on the whole value of the cable, importers can no longer undercut local players and aluminum building wire has gained pricing / margin over the last three months, while nothing changed for copper. LATAM margins are normalising in Colombia and Argentina after a two-year spike; Europe is mildly growing in volume and profitability, with some restructuring, capacity relocation and footprint moves planned, and significant growth is expected in the US. Recycled content reached 25% in Q2, lowering reliance on the tight US copper market.
quarterly_data.figure: aluminum cable tariff 25% on the whole value of the cable

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Massimo Battaini: Prysmian completed the industrialization of hollow-core fiber (data conveyed through air, 30% faster than standard glass) and, in the US, handed the fiber in cables to Amazon for an installation trial, which it passed; production, currently in Europe, will now be scaled, with Claremont, North Carolina the ideal place for extra capacity. Hollow-core will never exceed 10% of fiber market demand, but demand is high and margins 'extremely interesting'; towards the end of 2026 Prysmian will probably evaluate additional ownership in Relativity Networks.

CEO Massimo Battaini: a 32% Vitality Index means one third of revenue, EUR 7 billion, comes from products launched in the last three years. Prysmian analysed many companies over the last 12 months and stays open to M&A in spaces adjacent to cables, with the US probably the best geography; a perimeter change could come before the new Capital Markets Day, which will set out the 2027-2030/2031 trajectory.
